description: Complete the iOS host side and document the step. Update native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift so the app declares, loads and launches the PS1 core (PCSX ReARMed) with a real fullpath ROM and a populated system directory, surfacing a missing-BIOS/HLE condition in the HUD; and update SESSION_HANDOFF.md with the Phase 5 Step 2 section. The Swift compiles only in CI (no iOS SDK here), so it is written against the generated UniFFI signatures and reviewed by eye, exactly as the existing stub harness was. Depends on FEAT-002 (loader) and FEAT-003 (the core dylib is in the bundle). The stub harness view may be kept alongside or superseded; if superseded, keep the code path that still loads the stub available or justify its removal in the handoff (the 15/15 wrapper harness gate is independent of the Swift and must remain green).
steps: In ContinuumApp.swift, add PS1 core constants mirroring the existing Stub enum: coreId (e.g. "pcsx_rearmed"), library "pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib", systems ["ps1"], geometry (PS1 base ~320x240, max ~700x576; aspect 4:3 = 4.0/3.0), targetFps ~59.94, audioSampleRate 44100, pixelFormat 0 (RGB565 - PCSX ReARMed's default; the engine will re-negotiate via SET_PIXEL_FORMAT and the descriptor is superseded by the core's real av_info on load, so this is only the pre-load hint). Note the declared numbers are a hint: sync_descriptor_from_core overwrites geometry/fps/sample_rate from retro_get_system_av_info after load.
Resolve the core path from Bundle.main.privateFrameworksURL (same as the stub) and verify FileManager existence, surfacing a legible status string if missing.

PS1 content declares need_fullpath, so the app must hand the core a REAL, openable file path (FEAT-002 made the loader forward it). For this step's harness, ship or stage a small PS1 content file to a real path in the app's writable area (temporaryDirectory or applicationSupportDirectory) and pass that path as the launch filename with empty rom bytes. If no test ROM is bundled, still write a placeholder file to a real path and rely on the HUD to report load failure legibly rather than silently - the point is the loader/path plumbing, since CI cannot boot a game anyway. Do NOT commit any commercial ROM or BIOS.

Populate the system directory: pass systemDir = applicationSupportDirectory (created if needed). Document in a comment that a PS1 BIOS (e.g. scph1001.bin) placed there raises compatibility, and that WITHOUT a BIOS PCSX ReARMed falls back to HLE (pcsx_rearmed_bios option / Config.HLE) and still boots at reduced accuracy. The app should detect and show in the HUD whether a BIOS file is present in the system dir, so a missing BIOS is a legible on-screen condition rather than a silent failure.

Call engine.declareCore, engine.loadNativeCore (coreId, libraryPath, systemDir, saveDir), then engine.launch, wrapping errors into the existing status HUD string exactly as startSession() does now. Keep the attach-callback ordering (start the session only after the renderer is attached), which the existing code already gets right.

Update the HUD text to reflect Phase 5 Step 2 (e.g. label 'Phase 5 step 2 - PCSX ReARMed (software)') and add the BIOS-present/HLE line. Preserve the diagnostic lines (status, gpu, frames/fps/dropped) since on a sideloaded build the HUD is the only diagnostic.

Do NOT introduce Swift that needs types the generated UniFFI facade does not expose. The facade already provides declareCore(CoreDeclaration), loadNativeCore, launch, tick telemetry, attachMetal. If any new engine method is genuinely required, it must be added in uniffi_api.rs in FEAT-002/003 first; this feature should need no new FFI. Match argument labels/order/types (Data vs Vec<u8>, Double vs Float) against the generated signatures the same way the existing file does.

Update SESSION_HANDOFF.md: add a '## 17. Phase 5 Step 2: the first real core (PCSX ReARMed, software)' section documenting: (a) why PS1/PCSX ReARMed first (de-risk loader+ROM+input+audio through the software path before MoltenVK); (b) the thin passthrough decision (Option 1) and that the switch-wrapper IoC FrameGate stays reserved for the future Switch engine and is NOT on the PS1 path; (c) the environment commands added to native_core.rs and why each (SET_PIXEL_FORMAT mandatory + the accept-as-noop option families + GET_VARIABLE returning defaults); (d) the pixel-format negotiation approach (core chooses RGB565 by default / XRGB8888 via option; video() now reports the negotiated format instead of hardcoding Rgba8888); (e) BIOS handling (system dir population, HLE fallback, HUD surfacing); (f) need_fullpath and the fullpath plumbing; (g) the build-core.sh iOS strategy (platform=ios-arm64, DYNAREC=0 interpreter-first tradeoff, pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib), and the artefact-path chain across build-engine.sh / project.yml / package-ipa.sh / ios.yml; (h) explicitly, what remains UNPROVEN - the actual on-device PS1 boot, which CI cannot verify (CI only proves the macOS build produces a signed bundle embedding the core dylib). Follow the doc's existing tone; do not use em dashes.

Because Swift cannot be type-checked here, run `swiftc -frontend -parse native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift` if a Swift toolchain is present (treat as a spell-check only, per SESSION_HANDOFF §16 - it will not catch UIKit type errors). Then run the Rust/harness gates to confirm nothing else regressed.
acceptance_criteria: ContinuumApp.swift declares, loads and launches a core with coreId matching FEAT-003's dylib, library filename pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib, systems ["ps1"], passing a real fullpath as the launch filename and applicationSupportDirectory as the system dir.
The HUD surfaces whether a PS1 BIOS is present in the system dir and reflects the HLE fallback, and shows the Phase 5 Step 2 label plus the existing diagnostic lines.
No new UniFFI methods are required by the Swift (or any that are, exist in uniffi_api.rs); argument labels/order/types match the generated facade.
SESSION_HANDOFF.md has a Phase 5 Step 2 section covering all eight points (a-h), including the explicit statement that on-device PS1 boot is unproven and only CI-buildable.
No commercial ROM or BIOS is committed to the repo.
cargo test, both aarch64-apple-ios checks, clippy, and ./native/switch-wrapper/build.sh host all still pass.
If a Swift toolchain is available, swiftc -frontend -parse accepts ContinuumApp.swift.
findings:
Completed the iOS host side and documented Phase 5 Step 2. Two files changed: native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift and SESSION_HANDOFF.md. No new UniFFI methods were needed; the Swift uses only declareCore(CoreDeclaration), loadNativeCore, launch, and the attach/telemetry surface that already exist in uniffi_api.rs.

ContinuumApp.swift:
- Replaced the Stub enum with a PS1 enum: coreId 'pcsx_rearmed', library 'pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib' (matches FEAT-003's canonical filename exactly), systems ['ps1'], geometry base 320x240 / max 700x576, aspectRatio 4.0/3.0 (Float), targetFps 59.94 (Double), audioSampleRate 44100, pixelFormat 0 (RGB565). Comments note these are pre-load hints: sync_descriptor_from_core overwrites geometry/fps/sample-rate from retro_get_system_av_info and SET_PIXEL_FORMAT re-negotiates the format, so native_core.rs video() reports the real one.
- startSession() (still called only from surfaceAttached, preserving attach-before-launch ordering) resolves the core from Bundle.main.privateFrameworksURL, checks FileManager existence with a legible HUD line if missing, then declareCore -> loadNativeCore(coreId, libraryPath, systemDir, saveDir) -> launch(coreId, contentId, rom: Data(), filename), matching the existing argument labels/order/types exactly (Data for rom, String path for filename).
- need_fullpath: writes a placeholder file to temporaryDirectory/continuum-ps1.cue and passes that real openable path as the launch filename with empty rom bytes (no commercial ROM bundled). A load failure is caught and shown on the HUD rather than blanking the screen.
- systemDirectory() returns applicationSupportDirectory (created if absent), passed as both systemDir and saveDir. biosStatus() scans it for the known PS1 BIOS filenames (scph1001.bin etc.) and produces a HUD line: 'BIOS: <name>' when present, 'BIOS: none, HLE fallback' when absent. A comment documents that a BIOS raises compatibility and that without one PCSX ReARMed falls back to HLE (pcsx_rearmed_bios / Config.HLE) and still boots at reduced accuracy. No BIOS is ever bundled.
- HUD: renamed StubHarnessView -> PlayerView, label now 'Continuum · Phase 5 step 2 - PCSX ReARMed (software)' (hyphen, no em dash), added the new @Published bios line between status and gpu, kept status/gpu/frames-fps-dropped diagnostic lines.
- No em dashes were introduced in any new comment or string (verified by grep); pre-existing prose comments retain the file's original style.

SESSION_HANDOFF.md:
- Appended '## 17. Phase 5 Step 2: the first real core (PCSX ReARMed, software)' after §16, covering all eight points: (a) why PS1/PCSX ReARMed first (de-risk loader+ROM+input+audio on the software path before MoltenVK, paraLLEl-N64 next); (b) thin passthrough Option 1, FrameGate reserved for the Switch engine and not on the PS1 path; (c) the added environment commands and why (SET_PIXEL_FORMAT mandatory, GET_VARIABLE returns defaults, the accept-as-noop families, and the two deliberate refusals); (d) pixel-format negotiation via the DIRECTORIES-style global and video() reporting the negotiated format; (e) BIOS/system-dir/HLE handling and HUD surfacing; (f) need_fullpath and the ContentHint.full_path plumbing; (g) the build-core.sh ios-arm64 / DYNAREC=0 interpreter-first strategy plus the five-file artefact chain for pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib; (h) an explicit statement that on-device PS1 boot is UNPROVEN and CI only proves the signed bundle embeds the core dylib. No em dashes in the new section (verified by grep).

VERIFICATION (all pass in this Linux sandbox): swiftc -frontend -parse native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift OK (spell-check only, per §16; a Swift toolchain is present at /usr/bin/swiftc); cargo test 74/74; cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings clean; cargo clippy --features native-core,uniffi-bindings --all-targets clean; ./native/switch-wrapper/build.sh host 15/15. The macOS/Xcode iOS build and on-device PS1 boot cannot run here and are verified by the orchestrator's CI afterward.
